evidence: Read full AR/TR/EN and supplied Quran context 1:1–3, then the complete canonical 18:38 and its available meanings. The Arabic expressly opens «ممَّا قصدنا له قوله عزوجل: بِسْمِ ٱللهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيـمِ», analyzes the bāʾ, derivation of اسم and الله, then the paired divine names and their meanings, and closes with Qatada’s interpretation of the same full basmala as divine self-praise and the example «قال جريرٌ الشَّاعر». This is the basmala of 1:1. The 18:38 quotation «لَّٰكِنَّاْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي» and expansion «لَكِنْ أَنَا هُوَ اللهُ رَبِّي» are introduced by «كما» as a morphological analogy for elision and assimilation in الله; this supporting comparison does not establish an additional primary verse association. Likewise discussion of الرحمن الرحيم remains within the basmala and does not separately establish 1:3. TR begins with the same full basmala and preserves the derivations, analogy, all named interpretations and Jarir ending; EN does likewise. Both translations therefore follow this source entry throughout. The complete live passage https://tafsir.app/nahaas-meanings/1/1 confirms the source sequence and mapping.

evidence: Read complete Arabic, Turkish, English and Quran context 1:1–4. The Arabic explicitly begins «قوله تعالى: الْحَمْدُ للَّهِ», contrasts الحمد and الشكر, explains the nominative’s scope and the utterance as praise, request and divine instruction. Its second explicit lemma is «وقوله جل وعز: رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ», with the lexical derivation of رب and competing senses of العالمين, ending «فالعالَم دالّ على أنَّ له خالقاً ومدبِّراً». These directly explain the two parts of canonical 1:2 «ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ». The hadith, ordinary examples المال لزيد / أنا جواد / أنا شجاع, and poetic citations illustrate those explanations and are not additional Quran targets. Both TR and EN preserve all these sections and the final etymology of عالم, with matching opening and second lemma; their mappings follow this Arabic entry. The complete author passage at https://tafsir.app/nahaas-meanings/1/2 independently confirms the source text and 1:2 assignment.

evidence: Read complete AR/TR/EN and Quran context 1:2–6; additionally retrieved full 40:16 with all available meanings to identify the supporting quotation. The entry opens «قوله تعالى: مَلِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ ويُقْرأ مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ», compares ملك / مالك, gives the reports explaining يوم الدين as الحساب and الجزاء, and ends by explaining why sovereignty is especially attributed to God on the resurrection day. This directly and continuously explains 1:4. The quote «لِّمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ» belongs to 40:16, but «واحتجوا بقوله تعالى» explicitly introduces it as evidence in the argument over ملك / مالك in 1:4; its lexical observation about مُلك supports that comparison and is not an independent primary treatment of 40:16. Ordinary examples مالك الناس / مالك الطير / مالك الريح and the poetic دينه / ديني line are illustrative. TR and EN both retain the opening reading comparison, supporting quotation, transmission chain, meanings of الدين and the final resurrection explanation; both follow this Arabic source. evidence: Read complete Arabic, Turkish, English and Quran context 1:3–7, plus full canonical 76:21–22 and 10:22 with all available meanings. The Arabic opens «قوله تعالى: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ ولم يقل نَعْبُدكَ لأن هذا أوكد», explains العبادة and word order, then expressly introduces the second clause «ثم قال تعالى: وإيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ». The ensuing repetition of إياك, shift from third-person praise to direct address, and final ellipsis «وإياكَ نستعين على ذلك» all concern 1:5. The quotes «وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَاباً طَهُوراً» / «إنَّ هَذَا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَاءً» (76:21–22) and «حَتَّى إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ» (10:22) are explicitly illustrative instances of pronoun/address shifts, paired with al-Aʿsha’s poetry. They supply rhetorical parallels and do not establish independent primary targets. Both TR and EN preserve both main clauses, all lexical/poetic examples, the Quran comparisons and the final ellipsis; their mappings follow this Arabic entry. The complete live author passage at https://tafsir.app/nahaas-meanings/1/5 independently confirms the sequence and 1:5 assignment.

evidence: Read complete AR/TR/EN, supplied Quran context 1:4–7, and full canonical 38:22, 41:17, 20:50 and 13:7 with all available meanings. The primary lemma is the full 1:6 «ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَاطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ». It is explained as تثبيتنا / أرشدنا, followed by a lexical excursus on هدى and then reports identifying الصراط المستقيم with the Book of God or Islam, ending with Jarir’s two poetic lines. The supporting verses are explicitly organized by lexical senses: «ومنه» for 38:22, «ويكون هدى بمعنى بيّن» with 41:17, «بمعنى ألهم» with 20:50 including its short alternative gloss, and «بمعنى دعا» with 13:7. The author closes this comparison with «وأصل هذا كله: أرشد، والمعنى: أرشدنا إلى الصراط المستقيم», returning to 1:6. Although the examples carry brief glosses, their function here is to illustrate the semantic range of هدى, not to introduce separate primary commentary sections or additional mappings. TR and EN both preserve the entire lexical excursus, all transmission reports and the closing poetry; both follow the Arabic source and its 1:6 target. The full live author passage at https://tafsir.app/nahaas-meanings/1/6 confirms that structure and assignment.
